---
title: "User guide"
description: "A complete guide to tidydiversity: installation, data preparation, concepts, code, figures, interpretation and reporting."
---

This guide explains how to use tidydiversity **and** what its results
mean. Each chapter follows the same plan:

1. **The concept**: the question, the theory and its key formula, with
   the original references.
2. **Code** to copy into RStudio, run on real, openly licensed field data
   shipped with the package.
3. **Figures and tables** made by that code.
4. **How to interpret them**, including what they do not show.
5. **How to report them**: a model paragraph for a paper, with the numbers
   filled in from the analysis.

| Chapter | You will learn | Main functions |
|---|---|---|
| [1. Install, run and prepare your data](guide-01-install.html) | Set up R and RStudio; the tidy data format; abundance and incidence data; converting spreadsheets | `div_hill()` |
| [2. Hill numbers, completeness and coverage](guide-02-hill-numbers.html) | What diversity is; orders q = 0, 1, 2; diversity profiles; sample coverage; completeness; Chao1 and asymptotic estimates | `div_hill()`, `div_coverage()`, `div_completeness()`, `div_estimate()` |
| [3. Fair comparisons](guide-03-fair-comparisons.html) | Rarefaction and extrapolation; size- versus coverage-based standardisation; reading confidence intervals | `div_rarefy()`, `div_standardise()` |
| [4. Beta diversity](guide-04-beta.html) | Gamma = alpha × beta; dissimilarities; turnover versus nestedness; distance decay | `beta_hill()`, `beta_pair()`, `beta_multi()`, `beta_decay()` |
| [5. Community composition](guide-05-composition.html) | Ordination and how to read biplots; PERMANOVA; dispersion; indicator species | `ord_fit()`, `beta_permanova()`, `beta_dispersion()`, `beta_indicator()` |
| [6. Functional and phylogenetic diversity](guide-06-dimensions.html) | TD, PD and FD on one Hill-number scale; functional redundancy; choosing tau | `div_estimate()`, `div_standardise()` with `type` |

**Where to start.** New to R: Chapters 1 and 2. Comparing sites or
treatments: Chapter 3 is essential. Comparing species lists: Chapters 4
and 5. Traits or phylogenies: Chapter 6.

**Going further.** The [tutorials](tutorials.html) apply these methods to
ants, frogs, butterflies, insects, mammals, birds and trees; the
[Reference](../reference/index.html) lists every function. To put
diversity on a map, use the companion package
[tidymapr](https://tidymapr.in4metrix.dev), whose
[user guide](https://tidymapr.in4metrix.dev/articles/user-guide.html)
covers mapping and spatial analysis.

**How to cite.** Run `citation("tidydiversity")` in R.
